answer: Brie goes best with fig jam, pears, honey and walnuts, on a plain baguette or water cracker. Sweet, juicy and crunchy partners give a mild, creamy cheese the contrast it's missing.

faq.q: What fruit goes with brie?
faq.a: Pears, apples, grapes, figs and apricots. Juicy fruit cuts the butterfat.

faq.q: What wine goes with brie?
faq.a: Champagne or sparkling wine first, then oaked Chardonnay or a light red like Pinot Noir or Beaujolais.

answer: Camembert goes best with baguette, apples, dry cider and other bloomy-rind cheeses. It's stronger and more mushroomy than brie, so pair it with crisp, fresh partners.

faq.q: Camembert or brie?
faq.a: Camembert is smaller, stronger and earthier. Choose it if brie tastes bland to you.

faq.q: What drink goes with Camembert?
faq.a: Dry Normandy cider is the classic; Chardonnay and Beaujolais work too.

answer: Aged cheddar goes best with crisp apples, chutney, whole-grain mustard, pickles and honey. Sharp, salty cheddar needs sweet or tart partners to balance it.

faq.q: What fruit goes with sharp cheddar?
faq.a: Apples above all, plus pears, grapes and dried cranberries.

faq.q: What drink goes with aged cheddar?
faq.a: Cabernet Sauvignon, dry cider, IPA or stout. Cheddar is one of the most drink-friendly cheeses.

seo_title: What Goes With Aged Gouda? 52 Pairings & Drinks
seo_description: Aged Gouda pairings that work: dark chocolate, apples, smoked almonds and dried fruit lead the list. All 52 ranked, the wines and beers to pour, and what to skip.
answer: Aged Gouda goes best with dark chocolate, apples, smoked almonds and dried fruit. Its caramel, butterscotch flavor and crunchy crystals suit sweet and toasty partners.

faq.q: Why is aged Gouda crunchy?
faq.a: Those crystals are amino acids that form as the cheese ages. They mean flavor, not a flaw.

faq.q: What wine goes with aged Gouda?
faq.a: Cabernet, Merlot or tawny port. Its caramel notes also love stout and Belgian dubbel.

answer: Manchego goes best with membrillo (quince paste), chorizo, Marcona almonds, olives and jamón. Spain's nutty sheep's cheese loves the salty, sweet and smoky foods it grew up beside.

faq.q: What is membrillo?
faq.a: A firm, sweet quince paste from Spain, sliced thin and laid on Manchego.

faq.q: What wine goes with Manchego?
faq.a: Spanish reds like Rioja or Tempranillo, dry rosé, or fino sherry.

answer: Comté goes best with walnuts, pears, hazelnuts, saucisson sec and baguette. Its brown-butter, nutty flavor pairs with more nuts and fresh fruit.

faq.q: Comté or Gruyère?
faq.a: Very similar mountain cheeses. Comté is a little sweeter and fruitier; Gruyère is a little saltier.

faq.q: What wine goes with Comté?
faq.a: Chardonnay, Champagne, Pinot Noir or Beaujolais.

answer: Parmigiano-Reggiano goes best with balsamic glaze, pears, dried figs, prosciutto and honey. Salty, savory crystals love sweet and tart partners from the same Italian region.

faq.q: How do you serve Parmigiano on a board?
faq.a: Break it into rough chunks with a short knife rather than slicing. The crystals show better.

faq.q: What wine goes with Parmigiano-Reggiano?
faq.a: Chianti, Lambrusco or Champagne.

answer: Pecorino Romano goes best with honey, black pepper, cherry preserves, olives and cured pork. It's very salty and sharp, so small pieces with sweet partners work best.

faq.q: Is Pecorino Romano too salty for a board?
faq.a: Not in small pieces. Serve it with honey or fruit preserves to balance the salt.

faq.q: What wine goes with Pecorino?
faq.a: Chianti, Sangiovese or a light Italian white.

answer: Gorgonzola goes best with pears, honey, walnuts, figs and dark chocolate. Sweet, juicy and crunchy partners tame blue cheese's salt and sharpness.

faq.q: Dolce or piccante Gorgonzola?
faq.a: Dolce is soft and mild, easier for guests; piccante is firmer and sharper.

faq.q: What wine goes with Gorgonzola?
faq.a: Port or a sweet dessert wine. Among dry wines, try an Italian red with some fruit.

answer: Stilton goes best with walnuts, honey, oatcakes, dried fruit and port. Its crumbly, salty richness needs sweetness and crunch.

faq.q: What drink goes with Stilton?
faq.a: Port is the classic. Stout and sweet dessert wine work too.

faq.q: Is Stilton a strong blue?
faq.a: Medium. It's creamier and milder than Roquefort, stronger than Cambozola.

answer: Fresh goat cheese goes best with honey, figs, pistachios, fresh berries and herbs. Sweet and crunchy partners soften its bright tang.

faq.q: What wine goes with goat cheese?
faq.a: Sauvignon Blanc, especially from the Loire. Dry rosé and sparkling wine work too.

faq.q: How do you serve chèvre on a board?
faq.a: Roll a log in herbs, nuts or pepper, or drizzle it with honey.

answer: Taleggio goes best with prosciutto, speck, crusty bread, pears and Riesling or Belgian ale. Its funky rind and mild, buttery center suit cured ham and fruity drinks.

faq.q: Does Taleggio smell strong?
faq.a: The rind does; the inside is mild and buttery. Let it breathe on the board.

faq.q: What drink goes with Taleggio?
faq.a: Off-dry Riesling, Belgian ale or Pinot Noir.

answer: Fresh mozzarella goes best with basil, olive oil, tomatoes, prosciutto and balsamic glaze. It's mild and milky, so bright, salty and herbal partners do the talking.

faq.q: Mozzarella or burrata?
faq.a: Burrata is mozzarella with a creamy center. Use mozzarella for skewers, burrata for a centerpiece.

faq.q: What wine goes with mozzarella?
faq.a: Light, crisp whites and dry rosé.

answer: Prosciutto goes best with melon, figs, fig jam, burrata, Parmigiano and pears. Sweet fruit and creamy cheese balance its silky saltiness.

faq.q: How do you arrange prosciutto on a board?
faq.a: Loose folds or ribbons, never flat sheets. Separate the slices so guests can pick one up.

faq.q: What wine goes with prosciutto?
faq.a: Prosecco, dry rosé, Pinot Noir or Chianti.

answer: Genoa salami goes best with provolone, pickles, olives, mustard and crackers. Mild, garlicky salami is a team player that works with nearly every cheese.

faq.q: What cheese goes with Genoa salami?
faq.a: Provolone, mild cheddar, Gouda and triple-crème.

faq.q: How do you fold salami for a board?
faq.a: Fold rounds in half, then in half again, and line them up in a 'river'.

answer: Soppressata goes best with fresh mozzarella, hot honey, giardiniera, provolone and olives. Its coarse, peppery fat loves cool cheese and tangy pickles.

faq.q: Is soppressata spicy?
faq.a: Calabrese soppressata is; Veneto-style is mild. Check the label.

faq.q: What wine goes with soppressata?
faq.a: Chianti, Malbec or Cabernet.

answer: Mortadella goes best with pistachios, burrata, focaccia, giardiniera and Grana Padano. Silky, mild pork needs crunch, creaminess and a tangy pickle.

faq.q: How do you serve mortadella on a board?
faq.a: Thin slices, folded, or thick cubes on picks with pistachios.

faq.q: What wine goes with mortadella?
faq.a: Lambrusco, Prosecco or Chianti.

answer: Smoked salmon goes best with cream cheese, capers, pickled red onions, dill and rye or blini. Creamy and briny partners balance its rich smoke.

faq.q: Is smoked salmon safe on a board?
faq.a: Keep it cold and set it out last. Serve within about two hours.

faq.q: What wine goes with smoked salmon?
faq.a: Champagne, Sauvignon Blanc or unoaked Chardonnay.

answer: Honey goes best with blue cheese, goat cheese, Pecorino, aged cheddar and walnuts. Sweetness softens salty and tangy cheeses.

faq.q: Which cheeses need honey?
faq.a: Salty or sharp ones: blue cheese, Pecorino and fresh goat cheese.

faq.q: Honeycomb or honey?
faq.a: Honeycomb looks better and doesn't run; a honey dipper works in a small jar.

answer: Apples go best with aged cheddar, aged Gouda, Gruyère, pecans and walnuts. Crisp, tart apple cuts fat and resets your palate between bites.

faq.q: How do you stop apples browning on a board?
faq.a: Toss slices in a little lemon juice or cut them last.

faq.q: Which apple is best for cheese?
faq.a: Crisp, tart apples like Honeycrisp, Pink Lady or Granny Smith.

answer: Dark chocolate goes best with aged Gouda, blue cheese, hazelnuts, dried cherries and sea salt. Bitter cacao loves caramel, salt and toasted nuts.

faq.q: What cheese goes with dark chocolate?
faq.a: Aged Gouda first, then blue cheese and aged cheddar.

faq.q: What drink goes with dark chocolate?
faq.a: Port, Cabernet, Malbec or stout.

seo_title: What Goes With Gouda? Best Pairings for Young Gouda
seo_description: Young Gouda pairings that work: crisp apples, summer sausage, spicy brown mustard and pecans lead the list, plus the beers and wines to pour and what to skip.
answer: Young Gouda goes best with crisp apples, summer sausage, spicy brown mustard, pecans and an amber ale. Mild, buttery Gouda needs sharp, salty or crunchy partners to give it some backbone.
serve: Cut young Gouda into thick slices or cubes after trimming off the wax: it is soft enough to slice cleanly and holds its shape on a board. Plan about 1 to 1.5 oz per guest if it shares the board with two other cheeses. Set it near the apples and the mustard, the two partners that help it most.

To make it a Gouda flight, add aged Gouda and smoked Gouda beside it and let guests taste young to old. To drink, pour an amber or brown ale, a fruity red like Beaujolais or Zinfandel, or a dry cider. Looking for the crunchy, caramel kind? See the aged Gouda pairings instead.
guide: Which Gouda to buy: our ranking of Gouda brands
/blog/best-gouda-brands/

faq.q: What fruit goes with Gouda?
faq.a: Crisp apples first, then pears and grapes. Their juice and acid freshen a mild, buttery cheese. Dried apricots and figs work too, especially with aged Gouda.

faq.q: What meat goes with Gouda?
faq.a: Summer sausage, honey ham and smoked turkey for young Gouda; prosciutto and salami for aged. Mild, salty, slightly smoky meats suit its buttery flavor.

faq.q: What wine goes with Gouda?
faq.a: Fruity, medium-bodied reds like Beaujolais, Pinot Noir or Zinfandel, or a dry Riesling. Amber ales and brown ales are just as good. Save Cabernet and port for aged Gouda.

faq.q: Is young Gouda different from aged Gouda?
faq.a: Yes. Young Gouda is aged a few months and is soft, mild and buttery. Aged Gouda spends a year or more aging and turns hard, sweet and crunchy with caramel notes, so it suits different pairings.

answer: Feta goes best with Kalamata olives, honey or hot honey, pita chips, pomegranate and fresh mint. Its sharp brine needs juicy, sweet or crunchy partners, and a crisp dry rose to drink.
serve: Serve feta as a whole slab, not crumbles: block feta packed in brine is creamier and holds its shape. Pat it dry, set it on a small plate, drizzle with olive oil and dried oregano, and let guests break off pieces. About 1 to 2 oz per guest is plenty, because it's salty.

Build a Greek corner around it: Kalamata olives, cucumber and cherry tomatoes, pita chips and a small bowl of honey or hot honey for drizzling. In summer, watermelon cubes with mint are the best bite on the board. To drink, pour a dry rose, Assyrtiko or Sauvignon Blanc.
guide: Which feta to buy: our ranking of feta brands
/blog/best-feta-brands/

faq.q: What fruit goes with feta?
faq.a: Watermelon is the classic, along with pomegranate, mango, figs and grapes. Juicy, sweet fruit balances feta's salt.

faq.q: What wine goes with feta?
faq.a: Crisp, high-acid wines: dry rose, Assyrtiko, Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio. Avoid big oaky whites and heavy reds, which clash with the brine.

faq.q: Does honey go with feta?
faq.a: Yes. Honey's sweetness softens feta's sharp salt, and baked or whipped feta with honey or hot honey is a modern favorite. Add a pinch of chili flakes or thyme on top.

faq.q: Is feta good on a charcuterie board?
faq.a: Yes, especially on Mediterranean or mezze boards. Serve a block rather than crumbles, and put olives, pita and fresh vegetables beside it.

answer: Havarti goes best with apples, grapes, honey ham, butter crackers and a cold lager or dry Riesling. It's mild and creamy, so pair it with fresh fruit and gentle, salty partners, not sharp cheese.
serve: Slice Havarti about a quarter inch thick or cut it into cubes. It's soft, so chill it until 20 minutes before serving to make clean cuts, then let it warm a little so it tastes buttery. About 1 to 2 oz per guest; it's the cheese kids and picky eaters reach for first.

Keep it away from strong blue cheese and aged cheddar, which drown it out. Put it next to apples, grapes, honey ham or smoked turkey and butter crackers, and add a small bowl of honey or fig jam. Dill Havarti is the one to pick with smoked salmon. To drink, pour a light lager, a dry Riesling or a dry cider.
guide: Which Havarti to buy: our ranking of Havarti brands
/blog/best-havarti-brands/

faq.q: What fruit goes with Havarti?
faq.a: Apples, grapes and pears. Fresh, juicy fruit adds the acid that a mild, creamy cheese lacks.

faq.q: What meat goes with Havarti?
faq.a: Mild meats: honey ham, smoked turkey and mild salami. Dill Havarti also goes well with smoked salmon.

faq.q: What wine goes with Havarti?
faq.a: A dry or off-dry Riesling, Chardonnay without much oak, or a light Pinot Noir. A cold lager or a dry cider works just as well.

faq.q: Is Havarti good on a charcuterie board?
faq.a: Yes, as the crowd-pleaser. It's mild, creamy and easy to slice. Balance it with one sharper cheese, like aged cheddar, placed on the other side of the board.

answer: Pears go best with blue cheese like Gorgonzola, brie, Parmigiano-Reggiano, walnuts and honey. Their juicy, mellow sweetness softens salt and funk. Firm Bosc pears hold up best on a board.
serve: Use Bosc or Anjou pears that give slightly at the neck. Slice them just before guests arrive, about a quarter inch thick, and toss the slices with a squeeze of lemon juice so they don't brown. One medium pear covers about 4 guests.

Fan the slices next to the blue cheese and the brie, the two cheeses they help most, with walnuts and a small dish of honey nearby. Pear, Gorgonzola and walnut is one of the best three-part bites there is. To drink, pour a late-harvest Riesling, a tawny port or a dry pear cider.
guide: More fruit for your board: the best fruit for a charcuterie board
/blog/charcuterie-board-fruit/

faq.q: What cheese goes with pears?
faq.a: Blue cheeses like Gorgonzola, Stilton and Rogue River Blue first, then brie, Comte, Parmigiano-Reggiano and aged cheddar. Sweet, juicy pear softens salty and funky cheese.

faq.q: Which pear is best for a cheese board?
faq.a: Bosc. It's firm, slices cleanly and stays crisp. Anjou is a good second. Very soft Bartletts are delicious but get mushy on a board.

faq.q: How do you keep pears from browning on a board?
faq.a: Toss the slices in a little lemon juice, or a mix of water and lemon juice, right after cutting. Slice them as close to serving time as you can.

faq.q: What wine goes with pears and cheese?
faq.a: Off-dry or late-harvest Riesling, Sauternes, tawny port or a sparkling wine. A dry pear cider is a great non-wine option.

answer: Fresh figs go best with prosciutto, goat cheese, Gorgonzola, honey, pistachios and balsamic. Their jammy sweetness balances salty ham and tangy or blue cheese. Halve them just before serving.
serve: Buy figs ripe, the day you serve them: they don't ripen after picking and bruise easily. Rinse gently, trim the stem and cut them in half from top to bottom to show the pink center. One or two figs per guest is plenty, because they're rich.

Set the halves cut side up next to the prosciutto and the goat cheese. For the best bite, wrap a fig half in prosciutto, or top it with a spoon of chevre, a drizzle of honey and chopped pistachios. Out of season, swap in dried figs or fig jam. To drink, pour Prosecco, a dry rose or a tawny port.
guide: More fruit for your board: the best fruit for a charcuterie board
/blog/charcuterie-board-fruit/

faq.q: What cheese goes with figs?
faq.a: Fresh goat cheese, Gorgonzola and other blues, brie, Manchego and burrata. Figs' jammy sweetness suits tangy, salty and creamy cheeses.

faq.q: What meat goes with figs?
faq.a: Prosciutto above all, plus jamon serrano, speck and coppa. Salty, silky cured ham against sweet fig is a classic pairing.

faq.q: When are fresh figs in season?
faq.a: Roughly June through September in the US. Outside that window, use dried figs or fig jam for the same flavor.

faq.q: What wine goes with figs?
faq.a: Prosecco or another sparkling wine, a dry rose, or a tawny port with blue cheese and figs. Their sweetness also suits an off-dry Riesling.

answer: Cream cheese goes best with smoked salmon and capers, hot pepper jelly, everything crackers and bagel chips. Its cool tang balances salty fish, sweet heat and garlicky crunch.
serve: For the classic holiday shortcut, set an 8 oz block on a small plate, pour about half a cup of hot pepper jelly over it and surround it with sturdy crackers. Let it sit out 15 to 20 minutes so it spreads, and serve within 2 hours. One block covers 8 to 10 guests as one of several spreads.

On a bagel or brunch board, soften it, swirl it into a bowl, and set smoked salmon, capers, thinly sliced red onion, cucumber and dill around it. Whipped or flavored cream cheese is easier to spread, and a cheese ball is the make-ahead version. To drink, pour a dry sparkling wine, a crisp white or a cold lager.
guide: Which cream cheese to buy: our ranking of cream cheese brands
/blog/best-cream-cheese/

faq.q: What can I put on cream cheese for a party?
faq.a: Hot pepper jelly is the classic, then fig jam, cranberry chutney, salsa, or smoked salmon with capers. Pour the topping over a block and serve it with crackers.

faq.q: What crackers go with cream cheese?
faq.a: Sturdy ones: everything crackers, bagel chips, butter crackers and pita chips. Thin water crackers can snap under a cold block.

faq.q: Is cream cheese good on a charcuterie board?
faq.a: Yes, as a spread rather than a slicing cheese. Serve it in a bowl or as a topped block, and keep it away from delicate aged cheeses, which it mutes.

faq.q: What wine goes with cream cheese?
faq.a: Dry sparkling wine, Sauvignon Blanc or a dry Riesling. Their acid cuts the richness. With pepper jelly on top, an off-dry Riesling handles the heat best.

answer: Summer sausage goes best with sharp cheddar, butter crackers, whole grain mustard, dill pickles and pepper jelly. Its smoky tang needs sharp cheese, a sweet-salty cracker and something tart.
serve: Slice it about a quarter inch thick, on a slight angle for bigger rounds, and peel off the casing if it's fibrous or waxed. Plan about 1.5 to 2 oz per guest when it's one of two or three meats. Unopened, most summer sausage is shelf-stable, which is why it's the star of holiday gift boxes; once sliced, treat it like any meat and serve it within 2 hours.

Build the classic gift-box plate around it: sharp cheddar and Colby Jack cubes, butter crackers, a pot of whole grain or spicy brown mustard, dill pickles and pepper jelly. To drink, a cold lager, a dry cider or a bourbon on ice suit its smoke.
guide: Which summer sausage to buy: our ranking of summer sausage brands
/blog/best-summer-sausage/

faq.q: What cheese goes with summer sausage?
faq.a: Sharp or aged cheddar first, then Colby Jack, baby Swiss, pepper jack and smoked Gouda. Firm, mild-to-sharp cheeses stand up to its smoke and tang.

faq.q: What crackers go with summer sausage?
faq.a: Butter crackers like Ritz are the classic. Wheat crackers, pretzel crisps and rye crisps work too.

faq.q: Do you take the casing off summer sausage?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Many summer sausages have a fibrous or plastic casing that isn't meant to be eaten. Natural casings are edible but can be chewy, so peeling is still easier.

faq.q: What drink goes with summer sausage?
faq.a: Cold lager, amber ale, dry hard cider or bourbon. For wine, a fruity Zinfandel or a Beaujolais handles the smoke and spice.

seo_title: What Goes With Caviar? Blini, Chips, Champagne & More
answer: Caviar goes best with warm blini, crème fraîche, buttered brioche toasts and plain kettle chips, with Champagne or ice-cold vodka. Keep partners mild, rich and plain so the caviar leads.
serve: Keep the tin on ice until serving and use a non-metal spoon, such as mother-of-pearl, horn, wood or plastic, since silver and stainless steel can leave a metallic taste. Plan about 1 oz per person as a tasting, or half an ounce each when it's one item on a larger board. Open it just before guests arrive.

Set out warm blini or brioche toasts, a bowl of crème fraîche or mascarpone, and chives. For the high-low version, put a dab of crème fraîche on a plain kettle chip and add a small spoon of caviar. Smoked salmon makes a good second fish. Pour dry Champagne, cava or chilled vodka.
guide: Which caviar to buy: our guide to affordable caviar
/blog/best-caviar/

faq.q: How do you serve caviar at a party?
faq.a: Keep it on ice, serve it with a non-metal spoon, and set out blini or toast, crème fraîche and chives. About half an ounce to an ounce per person is plenty.

faq.q: Why do people eat caviar with potato chips?
faq.a: Salty, crunchy and plain, a potato chip carries caviar without competing with it, and the fat and crunch contrast with soft, briny pearls. Add a dab of crème fraîche.

faq.q: What drink goes with caviar?
faq.a: Dry Champagne or another dry sparkling wine, or ice-cold vodka. Avoid oaky or tannic wines, which clash with the brine.

faq.q: Why not use a metal spoon for caviar?
faq.a: Silver and some metals can give delicate caviar a metallic taste. Mother-of-pearl, horn, bone, wood or plastic spoons are neutral.

seo_title: What Cheese Goes With Grapes? Best Pairings & Drinks
answer: Grapes go best with brie, Manchego, aged cheddar, blue cheese and prosciutto. Cool, juicy sweetness cuts fat and salt, so they suit almost every cheese and cured meat on a board.
serve: Wash and dry grapes well, then cut them into small clusters of 5 to 8 with kitchen scissors instead of pulling them off the stem: clusters look better and stay fresher. Plan about a quarter cup, or 8 to 10 grapes, per guest. Mix red and green for color.

Tuck clusters into gaps next to the cheeses they help most, brie and blue cheese, and next to the prosciutto. For a winter board, roast grapes at 425°F for about 15 minutes with olive oil and thyme and serve them warm with ricotta or brie. To drink, sparkling wine, a dry Riesling or a rosé matches their bright fruit.
guide: More fruit for your board: the best fruit for a charcuterie board
/blog/charcuterie-board-fruit/

faq.q: What cheese goes with grapes?
faq.a: Brie and other soft cheeses first, then Manchego, aged cheddar, Gouda and blue cheese. Grapes' juice and acid balance creamy, nutty and salty cheeses alike.

faq.q: Red or green grapes for a charcuterie board?
faq.a: Both. Red grapes are a little sweeter and look rich; green grapes are crisper and more tart. A mix adds color.

faq.q: How far ahead can you put grapes on a board?
faq.a: Wash and cluster them a day ahead and keep them in the fridge. Add them to the board just before serving so they stay cold and plump.

faq.q: What meat goes with grapes?
faq.a: Prosciutto and other cured ham, plus salami and soppressata. Salty, fatty meat and cool, sweet fruit balance each other, the same idea as prosciutto and melon.

answer: Medjool dates go best with blue cheese, fresh goat cheese, Parmigiano-Reggiano, prosciutto and pistachios. Their caramel sweetness balances salty, tangy cheese, and they're perfect stuffed and wrapped.
serve: Slit each date lengthwise and pull out the pit. Serve them plain, or stuff them with a small spoon of goat cheese or blue cheese, a nut or a chunk of Parmigiano. Plan 1 to 2 dates per guest, because they're rich. Medjools are soft and sticky, so set them on a small plate or a corner of the board.

For the warm version, wrap stuffed dates in half a slice of prosciutto and bake at 400°F for about 10 to 12 minutes, until the ham crisps. Sprinkle with flaky salt or chopped pistachios. To drink, pour tawny port, an amontillado sherry or a dry sparkling wine.
guide: Which dates to buy: our ranking of Medjool dates
/blog/best-medjool-dates/

faq.q: What cheese goes with Medjool dates?
faq.a: Blue cheese like Gorgonzola or Stilton, fresh goat cheese, Parmigiano-Reggiano and Manchego. Salty and tangy cheeses balance the date's caramel sweetness.

faq.q: What do you stuff dates with?
faq.a: Goat cheese, blue cheese, a chunk of Parmigiano, an almond or pistachio, or peanut butter. Wrap them in prosciutto or bacon for a warm appetizer.

faq.q: Are Medjool dates good on a charcuterie board?
faq.a: Yes. They're one of the best sweet elements for a board, especially beside blue cheese and cured ham, and they keep well at room temperature.

faq.q: What wine goes with dates and cheese?
faq.a: Tawny port, sherry and dry sparkling wine. Nutty, raisined flavors echo the date, and bubbles cut its stickiness.
